questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I’ve always dreamed of studying abroad, so the key aspects for me were the chance to access better academic and career opportunities and to immerse myself in a completely new culture. I wanted a destination where I could grow both personally and professionally while experiencing life from a different perspective.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus is a great to feel part of the university community. Just be ready for shared facilities, occasional noise, and cultural differences in how people live. Being flexible and communicating with roommates makes the experience smoother.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process wasn’t the easiest, as some of the steps were unclear at first. However, with guidance from staff, I was able to complete it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The main support available was through email. Each time I reached out, the staff replied and provided clear guidance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wasn’t very successful in registering for the classes I originally wanted. While applying from Denmark, Competition Law was my first priority, but when I arrived at QUB I was told that it was no longer offered for undergraduates. I was disappointed because I had really looked forward to taking it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise future exchange students to double-check course availability before arriving, as some classes may change or be removed without clear notice. It’s also helpful to have backup course options and to contact the university early if you have questions, since they usually respond quickly by email.

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took BA-level courses, including International Trade Law, Law and Technology, and Commercial Law. The classes were undergraduate level and generally manageable, though each required consistent reading and engagement with the material.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at Queen’s University Belfast was quite different from UCPH. At QUB, the classes were more lecture-based with a stronger focus on structured teaching, whereas UCPH typically encourages more independent learning and student participation.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At my host institution, there were a variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities for students. Cultural activities included events, workshops. Socially, there were student societies, clubs, and informal gatherings that made it easy to meet other students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining the student societies. They are a great way to meet new people, make friends quickly, and get involved in social and cultural events on campus. Participating in societies really helps you feel part of the university community.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend that visiting students use their weekends and holidays to explore both Belfast and other cities in Northern Ireland and beyond. Sightseeing, visiting historical landmarks, and exploring local culture are all great ways to make the most of your time. Traveling to nearby cities also gives you a broader perspective on the country and its culture.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the local culture at my exchange site was fairly easy. Most people were extremely friendly and welcoming, and I found it easy to adapt to daily life and social norms. Of course, there were small differences compared to home, but overall the transition was smooth.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My main tip would be to get involved in student societies and campus events, as these are great places to meet local students. Being open, approachable, and willing to join group activities really helps in building connections.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most cultural differences were easy to adapt to, but one thing I found a bit challenging was the different communication style. Overall, it was a good learning experience.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I most appreciated how welcoming and helpful people were. From staff to everyone, everyone was approachable and willing to assist, which made settling in much easier and more enjoyable.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Check course availability in advance: Some courses may no longer be offered, so have backup options ready.

Get involved in student societies: They’re a great way to meet people, make friends, and experience campus life.

Be open and flexible: Adapting to cultural differences and new ways of learning will make your experience more enjoyable.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I’d advise future students to explore beyond academics, join societies, attend events, and travel a bit to get the full experience. Keep in mind that some courses may change, so have backup options. Planning ahead, being open to new experiences, and asking for help when needed will make settling in much easier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me, the most rewarding part was the opportunity to grow both personally and academically. Engaging with students from different backgrounds, discovering new perspectives, and adapting to a different way of learning helped me gain confidence and independence.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was managing finances. Living abroad can be expensive, but with careful planning, I was able to manage it successfully.
